$comment: Seirin cast — OPEN QUESTIONS, not answers. Records what the design document fixes (name, age, role, faction) and asks the questions whose answers become the visual design. Answers come from the project owner or a design agent, NOT the art agent. PRIMARY QUESTION SET is ai_agent_docs/Character_Design_Brief_AI_Agent_Questionnaire.md (sourced to 27 primary sources). The sections below are the WARDROBE-AND-REALITY SUPPLEMENT that the questionnaire does not cover — see ../references/wardrobe-questions.md.
status: UNANSWERED — no character below has an approved visual design yet.

how_to_use.1: Read the question set in question_template. It applies to every character.
how_to_use.2: Answer per character, in this file, replacing null. Short answers are fine.
how_to_use.3: An answer is only 'canon' once the project owner approves it. Mark approved:true.
how_to_use.4: The art agent may NOT invent answers. If a field is null, it asks. There is no linter for this — a human reviewer is the gate.

note_on_canon: The existing design document is a draft and is itself AI-generated. Treat it as a starting point to interrogate, not as canon. Where it conflicts with a better answer, the better answer wins — record the change.

wardrobe: What does this person actually wear on an ordinary working day, given their job?
Where do their clothes come from — inherited, issued, bought cheap, made, stolen?
What do they wear when it rains? When it is cold? Seirin is a coastal city with real weather.
Do they own more than one outfit? Which ones, and when does each get worn?
What is worn out, repaired, stained or too big? What does that say about their life?
Whose clothes are these really — do they fit, and were they chosen by this person?
wardrobe_sources: Which real garment tradition does this draw on? (See references/wardrobe-questions.md for the catalogue.)
Why would THIS person, in THIS city, plausibly own it?
What is the fastening, the layering, the weight of the cloth? Real clothes have construction.
If the answer is 'a bodysuit' or 'sci-fi armour' — why? Is that a decision or a default?
costume_plot: Scene by scene, what is this character wearing? (Costume-plot grid — see references/wardrobe-questions.md.)
Where does a costume change happen, and is there time for it in the story?
What gets wet, torn, borrowed or lost — and does it stay that way afterwards?
Who is on screen with them, and do they still read as distinct in that grouping?
function_and_climate: Does this outfit permit the actions the story asks of this character?
Seirin is coastal Honshu: what does this person wear in rain, in winter, in humid summer?
Which garment choices are explained by climate or region rather than by taste?
colour_zones: Main colour (メインカラー): which colour does this character MEAN, stated as a decision — separate from whatever covers the most area?
Zone by zone, what colour and why: Head/hair, Skin, Eye, Tops1 outer, Tops2 inner, Waist, Bottom1, Bottom2, Shoes, Decoration1 one-point accent, Decoration2 trim.
Head normally uses exactly 3 colours (hair, skin, eyes) and the body 8 or fewer. Does this character fit, and if not, why is the extra complexity earned?
Which single colour is reserved so that its appearance means something?
Judged at full sprite size rather than as swatches, does any large area read brighter or darker than intended (area effect)?
ensemble_colour: Coloured beside the whole cast rather than alone, does this character still separate — in hue AND in greyscale value?
What is this group's shared colour logic (faction, uniform, region), and how does this character deviate from it?
Which existing cast member is this character closest to in colour, and what is the deliberate difference?
physical_plausibility: If a height and weight are stated, do they survive arithmetic? Check BMI before it reaches a reference sheet.
What does this person's actual life — work, age, health, habits — do to their body?

primary_question_set.note: Answer this FIRST. It is derived from 27 primary sources with a principle-to-source attribution index, covering silhouette, kawaii/moe engineering, SD-chibi, physiognomic coding, transmedia flatness, worldview symbiosis, tiering, live-ops cadence, fan-art virality, merch and IP.
primary_question_set.supplement_rationale: It treats costume as a VARIABLE — how many variants per tier, what material — but never asks what the person actually wears on an ordinary day, where the clothes came from, or what they do in the rain. The sections in this file close that gap.
